summary:
Pará recorded 5 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, matching the Goiás/Maranhão band, and 5 in 2024 as well. Against a population of ~8.7 million the 2025 rate is about 0.57 per million per year, above the national average. Pará spans the Amazon region, where the dossier's finding that roughly two-thirds of killings happen outside the capitals means interior municipal exposure is hard to assess and protection infrastructure is thinner for a visitor travelling beyond Belém.

No Pará-specific legal or ordinance finding was identified; the risk signal is the sustained above-average killing counts and the Amazonian geography. A comparison point from the same dossier: Ceará recorded 8 killings in 2025 on a population of ~9 million.

sources.summary: ANTRA's 9th annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by SBT News): Brazil recorded 80 murders of trans and travesti people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; per-state 2025 counts - Ceara and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7 each, Goias, Maranhao and Para 5 each, Alagoas 2, Mato Grosso 3; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% Black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; Brazil has led the global ranking since 2008. Places Para in the five-killings band for 2025.

ANTRA 2024 dossier coverage (27 Jan 2025): 122 trans and travesti people murdered in Brazil in 2024, 16% below 2023's 145 and just under the 2008-2024 average of 125; five victims were human-rights defenders, including a city-council alternate; 95.9% of victims were travestis/trans women; worst states: Sao Paulo 16, Minas Gerais 12, Ceara 11, with no records in Acre, Rio Grande do Norte or Roraima; at least 68% (83 cases) occurred in interior cities outside state capitals; 1,179 killings confirmed 2017-2024; official statistics are unreliable due to misclassification and underreporting. Provides the 2024 national figures and interior-concentration pattern behind Para's context.
